title: CI: add numeric drift checks for INT8/FP8 vs FP16 baselines (small prompt set) + gating policy
author: Sahana Iyer
body:
Title: CI: add numeric drift checks for INT8/FP8 vs FP16 baselines (small prompt set) + gating policy

Context / Why
We’ve had a few recent cases where INT8/FP8 paths were “numerically correct” at the kernel level but still caused user-visible behavior changes (token divergence, increased hallucination rate on a subset of prompts). During the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we agreed we need a lightweight, repeatable correctness guardrail that runs continuously and fails fast on large drift.

This PR adds a GPU CI job that compares INT8 and FP8 outputs against a pinned FP16 baseline on a small, representative prompt set. It also wires in a gating policy so the drift check is required when changes touch quantized execution paths (or when explicitly opted-in via label).

What’s in this PR
1) New drift-check harness
- Adds a small prompt corpus (10 prompts) curated for quant sensitivity:
  - short factual Q&A (low entropy)
  - arithmetic / step-by-step reasoning style
  - code completion (indentation + symbols)
  - long prefill (2k-ish tokens) “needle” style
  - multilingual + mixed punctuation
- Fixed decode settings for determinism:
  - temperature=0.0 (greedy)
  - top_p=1.0
  - repetition penalty disabled
  - max_new_tokens=32
  - fixed seed
- Runs three modes on the same runtime build:
  - fp16 (baseline)
  - int8
  - fp8 (e4m3 accumulation policy as currently configured)

2) Metrics + thresholds (drift definitions)
We intentionally avoid “exact match only” since small numeric differences can legitimately change a later token; instead we gate on a combination of early-token stability + numeric similarity:
- Token stability (greedy decode):
  - For each prompt, compare generated token ids to fp16 for the first N=16 new tokens.
  - Thresholds:
    - INT8: must match fp16 for >= 9/10 prompts
    - FP8: must match fp16 for >= 8/10 prompts
- Logit similarity (per step, for the first 16 decode steps):
  - Compute cosine similarity between fp16 logits and quant logits at each decode step.
  - Thresholds (minimum over steps, then aggregated worst-case over prompts):
    - INT8: min cosine >= 0.9990
    - FP8: min cosine >= 0.9975
- Outlier protection:
  - Additionally gate on max absolute logit error (L∞) per step to catch rare blow-ups.
  - Thresholds:
    - INT8: L∞ <= 0.35
    - FP8: L∞ <= 0.75

Rationale for these numbers: they’re loose enough to avoid churn due to normal quant noise, but tight enough to catch regressions where kernel selection / scaling / alignment bugs cause systematic distortion. We can tune based on observed false positives from the next 1–2 weeks.

3) Baseline pinning + reproducibility
- Baseline is fp16 outputs generated on a pinned runtime commit and pinned model revision.
- The drift test includes the baseline metadata (runtime commit, model sha, tokenizer sha, prompt set version, decode params) in the output JSON.
- Adds a helper script to regenerate baselines locally in the perf-lab container image; CI does not regenerate baselines.

4) CI wiring + gating policy
- Adds a new GPU CI step: quant_drift_check (A100 runner)
  - Runtime: uses the standard CI CUDA container
  - Expected runtime: ~6–9 minutes depending on runner load
- Gating policy:
  - Required if any files match:
    - runtime/quant/**
    - runtime/kernels/**
    - runtime/attention/**
    - runtime/scheduler/** (only when quant_mode is touched)
  - OR if the PR is labeled: require-quant-drift
  - Not required for docs-only / non-runtime changes.

5) Developer ergonomics
- When the check fails, CI prints:
  - per-prompt token mismatch counts
  - the worst offending decode step
  - a short “next actions” section (rerun with --dump_logits, run with fp16-only, check scaling config, etc.)
- Uploads artifacts (JSON) for debugging:
  - drift_summary.json
  - per_prompt_metrics.json

Changed areas (high level)
- ci/steps/quant_drift_check.sh: runner entrypoint
- ci/policies/required_checks.yaml: gating rules for when the step becomes required
- runtime/tests/quant_drift/: prompt set, harness, thresholds
- runtime/tools/quant_baseline/: baseline generation + metadata stamping
- runtime/common/determinism/: seed handling consolidated so drift check is stable

Illustrative snippet (threshold config)
quant_drift_thresholds.yaml:
- int8:
  - token_match_prompts_min: 9
  - token_prefix_len: 16
  - min_logit_cosine: 0.9990
  - max_logit_linf: 0.35
- fp8:
  - token_match_prompts_min: 8
  - token_prefix_len: 16
  - min_logit_cosine: 0.9975
  - max_logit_linf: 0.75

Testing
- Local (A100): ran drift check 5x; stable pass, variance only in later-token divergence for FP8 on 1 prompt, within thresholds.
- CI: new step passes on this PR; artifacts uploaded.

Rollout / Risk
- This is a new CI requirement for a subset of PRs (quant-related path filters + opt-in label). Primary risk is test flakiness due to runner contention or non-determinism.
Mitigations:
- Greedy decode + fixed seed
- Warmup run included (first prompt ignored for metrics; still logged)
- Retry-once in the step wrapper if CUDA OOM or transient runner errors are detected
- Logs include runner GPU clocks + driver info to correlate issues

Follow-ups
- Expand to an H100 runner once capacity is available (will likely tighten FP8 thresholds separately per SKU).
- Add a small prefill-only activation drift probe to catch regressions earlier than decode divergence (requires additional runtime hooks).
- Consider a nightly “expanded corpus” job (50–100 prompts) that is non-blocking but pages on large drift.

References
- Linear: ENG-24819
- Customer signal: SUP-6194 (quality concerns suspected around FP8 path; this adds a guardrail to prevent repeats)

Commits (squash merged)
- runtime/tests: add quant drift harness + prompt corpus
- ci: add quant_drift_check step + required-checks policy
- tools: baseline generator + metadata stamping
- docs: add README for drift check (how to run + how to update baseline)

Review notes / Discussion highlights
- Grace: asked to ensure we don’t block non-quant changes. Updated required_checks.yaml to only trigger on quant/kernel/scheduler paths or explicit label.
- Arjun: requested thresholds rationale + a path to tuning. Added thresholds doc + aggregated metrics explanation in README.
- Jonas: flagged determinism concerns (tokenizer/model revisions). Added explicit model/tokenizer sha pinning and surfaced them in output JSON.
- Connor: requested failure mode guidance for release train. Added CI failure output hints and suggested rollback knob (force fp16) for emergency mitigation.

CI status
- build-and-unit-tests: pass
- gpu-smoke: pass
- quant_drift_check (A100): pass
- lint: pass

Merge outcome
Merged to main via squash on 2025-10-10.
